features.title: Per-class intervention counts in the escalation fold
features.spec:
Repository: kranz (Rust workspace). File: `crates/engine/src/escalation_metrics.rs`. This module already defines the single operator-intervention set used by the published autonomy ratio. In `mission_escalation` (around lines 268-327) a loop increments one `interventions: u64` for four classes: (1) grant decisions, `EventKind::GrantApproved` / `GrantDenied`; (2) steers, `EventKind::UserMessage` whose seq is >= the first `PlanApproved` seq; (3) revision rulings, `PlanRevised` / `PlanRevisionRejected`; (4) operator unblocks, `MilestoneUnblocked` where `!is_engine_lift(reason, block_context.as_ref())`. Do NOT define a second intervention set anywhere, and do NOT change which events count.

Add, in this file:
1. `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] pub struct InterventionCounts { pub grant_decisions: u64, pub steers: u64, pub revision_rulings: u64, pub operator_unblocks: u64 }` with `pub fn total(&self) -> u64` (the sum). Doc-comment each field with its class rule.
2. `pub fn mission_interventions(mission_id: &str, events: &[Event]) -> InterventionCounts`. It filters to `mission_id` and classifies exactly as the existing loop does. Refactor `mission_escalation` so its classification comes from this one place (e.g. the loop increments the per-class struct and `interventions` becomes `counts.total()`; or `mission_escalation` calls `mission_interventions`). The steer ledger rows must still be produced exactly as now. Optionally keep the counts on `MissionEscalation` as a private field.
3. `pub fn format_intervention_classes(counts: &InterventionCounts) -> String` returning exactly `"{s} steer(s), {g} grant decision(s), {r} revision ruling(s), {u} operator unblock(s)"`, singular when the count is 1 and plural otherwise. Examples: `2 steers, 1 grant decision, 0 revision rulings, 0 operator unblocks`; `0 steers, 0 grant decisions, 0 revision rulings, 0 operator unblocks`; `1 steer, 0 grant decisions, 0 revision rulings, 1 operator unblock`. The report and the CLI will both use this one renderer.

Tests go in the existing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` of this file, reusing its `ev`, `created`, `sample_plan` helpers. EVERY new test name must start with `intervention_classes_` (that prefix must not already exist in the repo; check with grep). Do not rename or edit existing tests. Run `cargo test -p kranz-engine --lib intervention_classes_` and `cargo test -p kranz-engine --lib escalation_metrics` and show both outputs as evidence. Run `cargo fmt --all` and `cargo clippy -p kranz-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`. Do not touch `events.rs` or `types.rs`.

features.spec:

It already has `TerminalOutcome::Abandoned` (an operator-retired mission, kept out of the autonomy denominator), `InterventionCounts`, `mission_interventions(mission_id, events)` and `format_intervention_classes`. Read the whole file first.

Add:
1. `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] pub struct AbandonedMissionRow { pub mission_id: String, pub interventions: InterventionCounts, pub total_interventions: u64, pub features_completed_before_abandon: u64, pub delivered_before_abandon: bool }`. `features_completed_before_abandon` counts `EventKind::FeatureCompleted { .. }` events whose seq is lower than the FIRST `MissionAbandoned` event's seq. `delivered_before_abandon` = that count > 0.
2. `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] pub struct AbandonedMissions { pub missions: u64, pub delivered_before_abandon: u64, pub total_interventions: u64, pub rows: Vec<AbandonedMissionRow> }`, with rows sorted by mission_id. Doc-comment that this figure sits BESIDE the autonomy ratio and never feeds it.
3. `pub fn abandoned_mission_row(mission_id: &str, events: &[Event]) -> Option<AbandonedMissionRow>`: None unless the mission's terminal outcome (same first-terminal rule as `mission_escalation`) is Abandoned. Interventions come from `mission_interventions`.
4. `pub fn summarize_abandoned(rows: Vec<AbandonedMissionRow>) -> AbandonedMissions`: sorts the rows and sums them.
5. Add `#[serde(default)] pub abandoned: AbandonedMissions` to `EscalationMetrics`. In `aggregate`, collect `abandoned_mission_row` for each mission and set the field. The `Some(TerminalOutcome::Abandoned) | None => {}` arm must still not touch any autonomy counter. Do NOT change `AutonomyMetric`, `closed_missions` or any existing computation.
Update the module doc comment to list the abandoned figure as a companion to metric 1.

- `abandoned_missions_fold_no_feature_is_not_delivered`
- `abandoned_missions_fold_feature_after_abandon_not_counted` (a FeatureCompleted with seq after the abandon is ignored)
- `abandoned_missions_fold_completed_and_failed_excluded` (completed and failed missions produce no row; empty input gives AbandonedMissions::default())
Construct `EventKind::FeatureCompleted` with the fields defined in `crates/engine/src/events.rs` (around line 292). Read it, but do not edit events.rs or types.rs. Run `cargo test -p kranz-engine --lib abandoned_missions_fold_` and `cargo test -p kranz-engine --lib escalation_metrics`, and show the outputs. The REST handler in crates/server serializes EscalationMetrics, so run `cargo test -p kranz-server --lib` too and report the result. Run fmt and clippy on kranz-engine.
